messages:
maria.g: Hey @sam.k @kevin.b — customer acme-corp hit a streaming bug. Client reconnects quickly after a network blip and the final SSE chunk is gone, leaving an incomplete JSON and no finish_reason. repro below.

sam.k: thanks — can you paste the minimal repro + headers?

maria.g: here we go. They call the /v1/stream endpoint, get events until about token N, then client reconnects within ~150ms. On reconnect the server resumes but the previous stream's last event wasn't flushed to the proxy/client, so the client sees truncated JSON.

maria.g: repro steps (short):
1) start stream: curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream" -d "{\"model\":\"rwd-1\",\"input\":\"long prompt\"}"
2) mid-output, simulate network blip and immediate reconnect (client opens new connection within 100-200ms)
3) new connection receives a partial last-data event (truncated JSON) and then new tokens — client JSON.parse -> fails

maria.g: sample captured SSE sequence (as received by client after reconnect):
```
event: message
data: {"id":"c3","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...final fragment starts but ends mid-utf8"}}]

data: {"id":"c4","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"more tokens"}}],"finish_reason":null}
```

maria.g: notice the first data payload above is cut off (no closing braces) and then a new data arrives. JSON becomes: `{"id":"c3","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...final fragment starts but ends mid-utf8"}}]\ndata: {"id":"c4"...` -> parse error.

kevin.b: interesting. Do we have proxy logs? which layer is doing streaming (fastly/nginx/edge LB)?

maria.g: customer is behind Fastly + our hosted endpoint (us-east). I asked them to attach flow logs, they sent the following excerpt: 
```
[proxy] conn 10.20.30.x - reset after 120ms, downstream idle timeout
[redwood] stream session 0x7f3a flush 0 bytes -> connection closed
```

sam.k: could be the proxy closing on idle and the runtime's last buffered chunk not flushed. If client reopens immediately, it may get both a broken tail + new stream. We had a similar report months ago but this one is more sensitive due to quick reconnect.

maria.g: customer sees `finish_reason` missing on the last logical choice; sometimes they get `finish_reason:null` on the next event but it's a separate data frame so client parsing fails.

kevin.b: workaround suggestion for customers: implement a short backoff before reconnect (200-500ms) and make client resilient to encountering partial events by using a framed parser tolerant of broken chunks. On our side we should consider ensuring final chunk is flushed with a short TCP FIN on stream close or add a `session_end` sentinel event.

sam.k: logging/action items: 1) ask infra for fastly config: idle timeout / proxy buffer flush behavior 2) add additional telemetry to runtime to log `stream_flush` events and whether `last_chunk_flushed`==true 3) ask eng-runtime to consider emitting a guaranteed `__end__` event before closing (or adding `Content-Length`-style marker to SSE).

maria.g: customer troubleshooting: i gave them a temporary client-side patch (delay reconnect 300ms + tolerant parser). They confirmed it reduces occurrences.

support-bot: ticket #T-21098 created and linked to account acme-corp.

kevin.b: tagging eng-runtime for triage: @eng-runtime can you validate whether runtime flush uses tcp push + shutdown or relies on proxy to send trailing bytes? Also check if quantized kernel threads could be delaying final flush during preemption.

sam.k: thanks all. I'll attach request_id and example pcap that customer provided to the eng-runtime thread. Will follow up after infra confirms fastly settings. :thumbsup:
